summary: Steamboat Point lookout, Douglas County, OR: 15-foot tower built 1933 in Umpqua NF, staffed 1937, removed or destroyed 1965. No source describes the site now.

facts.design: 15-foot tower; L-5 per firetower.org and firelookout.com, L-4 cab per Oregon Lookouts
facts.status_note: Removed in 1965 per firetower.org, destroyed that year per firelookout.com. No source describes what remains.

staffing.status: staffed in 1937 (Jack Hutchins returned to the station)

events.note: 15-foot tower built one half mile west of the summit
Roseburg Chieftain reported the CCC was to build a 14 x 14 lookout before snow; not confirmed as the structure built
Panorama photographs taken by Lester Moe, August 19, 1933
Jack Hutchins returned to resume lookout work after a few weeks fighting a fire at Randle, Washington (Roseburg News-Review, August 17, 1937)
firetower.org: removed in 1965; firelookout.com: destroyed in 1965; Oregon Lookouts gives no year

evidence.supports: built 1933 one half mile west of the summit; 15-foot pole L-5 tower; removed 1965
evidence.quote: Built in 1933 one half mile west of the summit, this 15' pole L-5 tower was removed in 1965.
This 15' pole L-5 tower, built in 1933, was destroyed in 1965.

evidence.supports: CCC was to build a 14 x 14 lookout before snow (Roseburg Chieftain, September 14, 1933)
evidence.quote: A 14 x 14 lookout is to be constructed by the CCC before the snow flies.

evidence.supports: 1933 15-foot round fir timber tower with an L-4 cab
evidence.quote: 1933: A 15-foot round fir timber tower with an L-4 cab was constructed.

evidence.supports: panorama photos August 19, 1933 by Lester Moe
evidence.quote: August 19, 1933: Panorama photos taken by Lester Moe.

evidence.supports: 1937 Jack Hutchins returned to lookout work after Randle fire
evidence.quote: Jack Hutchins returned to Steamboat Monday to resume his work in the lookout station after spending the past few weeks at Randle, Wn., fighting the fire there.

evidence.supports: county list: Steamboat Point, Tower, Gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firetower.org and firelookout.com describe a 15-foot pole L-5 tower. Oregon Lookouts describes a 15-foot round fir timber tower with an L-4 cab. The brief's L-4 comes from Oregon Lookouts. The story reports both readings.
firetower.org says removed in 1965; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1965; Oregon Lookouts says removed with no date. The story gives 1965 and reports both words.

The FFLOS detail coordinates (43.347220 N, 122.712820 W) match the FFLOS county list (43.34722, -122.71282). The brief's alternate point (43.3461, -122.7244) comes from another dataset that was not checked here.

notes_for_editor: No source describes the site now; the brief's access 'unknown' is unresolved. Whether the CCC 14 x 14 lookout planned in 1933 is the structure built that year is unclear. Search results also show a different Steamboat Point lookout in Dayton, Wyoming; it was not used. The brief's alternate coordinates (43.3461, -122.7244) should be checked against their source before any map use.
